extraFacts.fact: A hose fitting's dash size is the hose inside diameter in sixteenths of an inch: -04 is 1/4 inch, -06 is 3/8 inch, -08 is 1/2 inch, -10 is 5/8 inch, -12 is 3/4 inch and -16 is 1 inch. A fitting must be matched to the hose construction and crimped to the diameter set for that hose and ferrule.
extraFacts.source: SAE J517 hose size convention; hose and fitting maker crimp data

extraFacts.fact: JIC 37° flare fittings (SAE J514, ISO 8434-2) and SAE 45° flare fittings (SAE J512) share thread sizes in several sizes but have different seat angles, 37° and 45°, and do not seal against each other. JIS B 8363 fittings use a 30° cone seat, 60° included, and a BSP parallel or metric straight thread. BS 5200 covers the BSP 60° cone connection.
extraFacts.source: SAE J514, SAE J512, JIS B 8363, BS 5200

extraFacts.fact: DIN 2353 24° cone connectors come in a light (L) and a heavy (S) series. Light and heavy fittings for the same tube size use different threads and do not mate. ORFS (O-ring face seal, SAE J1453, ISO 8434-3) fittings seal on an O-ring in a flat face, not on a cone.

SAE J518 (ISO 6162) four-bolt flanges come as Code 61, the standard-pressure series, and Code 62, the high-pressure series. For the same nominal size they have different bolt spacings and are not interchangeable.
NPT and NPTF tapered pipe threads seal on the thread; the pressure rating of a pipe-thread end falls with size, so at the larger sizes the end can limit an assembly below the hose rating.
extraFacts.source: SAE J514 pipe-thread connection ratings; ASME B1.20.1 / B1.20.3

extraFacts.fact: NPSM is the straight (parallel) pipe thread, mechanical; a female NPSM swivel seats on a 60° cone and so mates with a male NPT or NPTF nose, whereas NPTF is a tapered thread that seals on the thread itself. ORB is the SAE O-ring boss straight thread (SAE J1926-1) sealed by an O-ring.
extraFacts.source: SAE J476 and J516 (pipe-thread hose ends); SAE J1926-1; Parker 10743 Female NPSM (60° cone) entry in this shelf's range

extraFacts.fact: Steel hose fittings and hose couplings are normally classified under HS subheading 7307.99; the importer's customs broker has the final say.
